proposals.before: On the twenty-sixth Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. The Prince sent Li Cun'an and Rengong into Youzhou to calm the populace and seal the treasury, then appointed Rengong military governor of Youzhou, leaving a dozen trusted men including Yan Liude to share civil and military duties before returning himself.
proposals.after: On the twenty-sixth Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. The Prince sent Li Cunshen and Rengong into Youzhou to calm the populace and seal the treasury, then appointed Rengong military governor of Youzhou, leaving a dozen trusted men including Yan Liude to share civil and military duties before returning himself.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李存審 is Li Cunshen (審 shěn); Cun'an misreads the given name.

proposals.before: In the ninth month the emperor appointed Rengong acting Minister of Works and military governor of the Lulong circuit at Youzhou.
proposals.after: In the ninth month the emperor appointed Rengong acting Minister of Works and military governor of the Lulong Army circuit at Youzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 廬龍軍節度使 is Lulong Army military governor; “circuit at Youzhou” understates 軍.

proposals.before: On the fifth of the ninth month he halted at Anseijun.
proposals.after: On the fifth of the ninth month he halted at Anse Army.
proposals.reason: 安塞軍 is Anse Army; “Anseijun” is an untranslated romanization fuse.

proposals.before: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua (898) he sent his eldest son to seize Luzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. Rengong then held Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and petitioned the court for the command baton.
proposals.after: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua (898) he sent his eldest son to seize Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. Rengong then held Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and petitioned the court for the command baton.
proposals.reason: 淪州 denotes Cangzhou (滄州), Lu Yanwei's seat; Luzhou misreads the place name.

proposals.before: Si'an gave battle at Fanyang, feigning defeat and drawing back slowly. The Yan troops pursued to Neihuang, where Si'an's infantry formed line and wheeled to counterattack.
proposals.after: Si'an gave battle at Fanyang City (繁陽), feigning defeat and drawing back slowly. The Yan troops pursued to Neihuang, where Si'an's infantry formed line and wheeled to counterattack.
proposals.reason: 繁陽城 is Fanyang City near Neihuang and must not be confused with 范陽.

proposals.before: From the seventh month through the tenth Rengong sent more than a hundred envoys begging Jin for aid. The Prince then called on Yan for troops; Rengong sent his commanders Li Pu and Xia Houjing, overseer Zhang Juhua, secretary Ma Yu, and others with thirty thousand men to join the campaign.
proposals.after: From the seventh month through the tenth Rengong sent more than a hundred envoys begging Jin for aid. The Prince then called on Yan for troops; Rengong sent his commanders Li Pu and Xiahou Jing, overseer Zhang Juhan, secretary Ma Yu, and others with thirty thousand men to join the campaign.
proposals.reason: 夏侯景 is Xiahou Jing; 張居翰 is Zhang Juhan (翰 hàn), not Juhua.

decisions.reason: 李存審 is Li Cunshen; the current Cun'an does not match either the characters or their reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 武皇令李存審與仁恭入城

decisions.reason: Lulong circuit is an established and accurate English rendering of 廬龍軍; inserting 'Army circuit' is awkward and adds no useful distinction.
安塞軍 is Anse Army; Anseijun leaves 軍 fused and untranslated.
Lu Yanwei held Cangzhou, and the same sentence immediately lists 滄 among the acquired prefectures. Parallel text confirms 滄州, not Luzhou.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 劉仁恭遣其子守文襲滄州；彥威棄城

decisions.reason: Fanyang is the correct romanization of 繁陽. Adding Chinese characters to this isolated English place name does not correct an error and is inconsistent with the prose.
夏侯 is the compound surname Xiahou, and 張居翰 is Zhang Juhan; both current English forms are incorrect.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李溥夏侯景、監軍張居翰

claimRevisions.reason: The full English name claim must match the corrected reading Li Cunshen.
The given-name claim must change from Cun'an to Cunshen with the translation.
The name claim must preserve Xiahou as the compound surname.
The English name claim must match the corrected reading Zhang Juhan.
